system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. Seller labels it standard, agreed and final. | **25% / AUD 6m** general warranty cap. The 20% fallback requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost; none is given. | **Reject; propose AUD 6m.** The fallback is not authorised, and Seller’s assertions do not establish agreement or market terms. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with recovery only above the basket. | **AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket**, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; counter at playbook thresholds.** Seller’s proposed thresholds are materially higher and use a tipping point inconsistent with the buyer’s position. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | 18 months; Seller also proposes applying any limitation to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | **24 months after Completion** for general warranty claims; preserve separate regimes for other claim categories. | **Reject; propose 24 months.** The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits for administrative simplicity. | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap and at least six years**, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; require the separate regime.** Administrative simplicity is not a reason to dilute the playbook’s core title protections. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no effective fraud carve-out is stated. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Reject; add the full carve-out.** The playbook makes this non-waivable. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters found by prudent search. | **Reject general disclosure; retain only adequate specific disclosures.** A blanket reference does not identify matters fairly enough for the buyer to assess them. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including data-room or public-record matters. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusions. If any qualifier remains, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete the blanket exclusion.** It improperly sweeps in adviser knowledge and matters merely discoverable. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says final consent and condition-satisfaction evidence are absent. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer. | **Reject; make both conditions to Completion.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, and delivery alone does not establish conditions are met. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms no repayment or final discharge is included. | Current payout; repay directly from Completion funds and obtain effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject post-Completion release as drafted; require completion mechanics.** The facility remains outstanding and no final discharge is evidenced. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 bonuses are not separately itemised in the funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | DD-005 bonuses plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by Seller. | **Require a specific line item or Seller funding.** The disclosed conditional liability must not be silently omitted from the completion mechanics. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open but is not independent proof of non-payment; no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the room. | Broaden the narrow indemnity to address the transfer/ownership and related exposure, while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as verified either way. | **Reject the narrow scope; broaden and preserve cure rights.** The disclosure leaves payment and assignment unconfirmed, not resolved. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; Seller asserts no confirmed liability. | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates; assume neither confirmed breach/harm/notification duty nor a numeric demand. | **Require preservation, investigation and updates without prejudging outcome.** The disclosure leaves access, scope and notification status unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, avoidability, termination and accrual; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Seek diligence and assess under agreed price mechanics.** The disclosure does not establish that the renewals are unavoidable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; Seller says Tax/IP are settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate, with no hidden general-regime override. | **Reject the blanket override; keep Tax/IP open.** Seller’s wording risks collapsing distinct protections into the general regime without buyer authority. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence of 100% title. | Obtain independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; treat DD-012 only as a supplied internal source. | **Require independent verification.** A register supplied in diligence identifies the source relied on but does not independently verify title. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers Tax and IP settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms **open**; do not assume unlimited liability or that terms are resolved. | **Do not accept Seller’s characterisation; negotiate separately.** The playbook records these terms as open and provides no authority for settlement. |

Seller’s labels such as “standard,” “agreed,” “final” and “cleared” are assertions, not buyer approvals.
=== END ADVICE ===
